courses.title: IC101 — Onboarding onto Tools
courses.summary: Install Docker and set up the shared workbench: a Linux desktop that runs in a browser tab on your laptop, with the team's chip design tools and the SKY130 PDK. Every other course here requires it.

courses.title: IC102-A — Working in Tiny Tapeout Repos
courses.label: Analog, in Magic
courses.summary: Start a project from Tiny Tapeout's template, put the AD104 inverter in its tile, and get its layout through DRC, LVS and precheck.
courses.pick: Take this version for an ASIC Zoo cell, an analog block in CrossWalk or any other project where you draw the layout yourself and commit the GDS.

courses.title: IC102-D — Working in Tiny Tapeout Repos
courses.label: Digital, in Verilog
courses.summary: Start a project from Tiny Tapeout's template, replace its adder with an 8-bit counter and a test that catches a planted bug, and keep every workflow green.
courses.pick: Take this version for Sentry, HART-1 or any other project whose layout Tiny Tapeout's workflow builds from your Verilog.

courses.title: IC103 — PCB Design with KiCad
courses.summary: Draw a footprint in KiCad from a package drawing, lay out a Pmod for one project's pins, and take a board for a team chip as far as an orderable design.

courses.title: AD101 — Signals
courses.summary: Use notes and chords to learn to read signals in time and in frequency, and to see what a filter does to them.

courses.title: AD102 — Linear Circuits & Fabrication
courses.summary: Find out how resistors and capacitors are built on a SKY130 chip, and size your own to hit target values inside an area budget.

courses.title: AD103 — Nonlinear Circuits
courses.summary: Simulate a SKY130 diode and MOSFET in XSchem, find the MOSFET's regions of operation, and extract key parameters of each, such as the threshold voltage.

courses.title: AD104 — Layout
courses.summary: Plan cells as stick diagrams, draw them in Magic until they pass DRC and LVS, extract their parasitics, and place and route four standard cells by hand.

courses.title: AD201 — Analog Signal Processing
courses.summary: Filters, amplifiers and the op amp.

courses.title: AD202 — Mixed Signal
courses.summary: ADCs, DACs and the interface between analog and digital circuits.

courses.title: DD101 — Intro to Digital Logic
courses.summary: Build a NAND gate from two relays and every other gate from NAND, then turn truth tables into gate circuits and build a full adder.

courses.title: DD102 — Digital Logic & FPGAs
courses.summary: Type the full adder you drew in DD101 into SystemVerilog and test it, then chain four copies into a 4-bit adder and turn that into an FPGA bitstream.

courses.title: DD103 — RTL on FPGAs & ASICs
courses.summary: Learn more SystemVerilog by designing a 4-floor elevator controller from its state table, then take it through the open-source RTL-to-GDSII flow to a layout that passes DRC and LVS.

courses.title: DD104 — Pre-Silicon Verification
courses.summary: Write cocotb tests that catch all thirteen broken versions of SimProc, an 8-bit processor written by students on the team.

courses.title: DD105-A — Testbenches with UVM
courses.label: SystemVerilog and UVM, on Verilator
courses.summary: Build a UVM testbench for a small packet router until it catches all fifteen bugs planted in the design.
courses.pick: Take this version if you want to write the testbench in SystemVerilog, the same language as your RTL.

courses.title: DD105-B — Testbenches with UVM
courses.label: Python and pyuvm, on cocotb
courses.pick: Take this version if you want to keep writing tests in Python, as you did with cocotb in DD104.

courses.title: DD202 — Computer Architecture
courses.summary: Memory architecture and a simple computer.
